subject: Decision Bridge: Annual Planning & QBR Prep — alignment and fallback scenarios
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Decision Bridge: Annual Planning & QBR Prep — alignment and fallback scenarios

Team —

We need a short, operational thread to align on targets and the set of scenario plans we'll present at the July QBR. This is not a strategy write-up — it's an execution bridge so the execs can pick a decision and communicate to the company. Key asks up front:

- Confirm top-line targets for revenue, bookings, and ARR energy cost assumptions by EOD Wed (Jun 16).
- Owners for each scenario (Base / Conservative / Aggressive) — names and one-sentence leverage for the scenario.
- Bring any hard constraints (capacity, projected headcount, major vendor commitments) that would change the scenarios.

I've attached: DecisionBridge-Agenda.pdf (proposed 60-min sync), QBR-SCENARIOS-2027.xlsx (templates), and CostAssumptions_v3.csv (running numbers). Please review and reply with ownership / blockers.

Proposed meeting slot: Thu Jun 17, 10:00–11:00 PT. If you cannot make it, add a delegate and note the single required deliverable: a one-slide summary of your scenario and the one metric that would move us between Base and Conservative.

Thanks — short and direct here.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: DecisionBridge-Agenda.pdf (pdf), QBR-SCENARIOS-2027.xlsx (xlsx), CostAssumptions_v3.csv (csv)

> We need a short, operational thread to align on targets and the set of scenario plans we'll present at the July QBR. ...

Thanks Marcus — I like the clarity. Quick notes from Product/Go-to-market lens:

- I'll own the product-side scenario slides (feature velocity and release risk). Owner: Jonas Weber.
- For our numbers, product risk is mostly release cadence and GA delays; I'll map a probability wedge for each major milestone in the QBR spreadsheet.
- Constrain: the new model runtime kernel landing (internal stack) is a binary risk on our CPU-hour savings; if it slips >2 sprints we should plan pivot savings assumptions.

I can make the Thu 10:00 PT slot, but if Marissa needs to shift because of customer meetings, propose Fri Jun 18, same time.

I'll upload an initial 'risk wedge' tab to the QBR-SCENARIOS spreadsheet by EOD Wed.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP Product, Redwood Inference

I can't do Thu 10:00 PT (customer demos). Fri Jun 18, 10:00–11:00 PT works for me.

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Decision Bridge — final slot and pre-work checklist

Thanks for the quick turn. Final decisions:

- Meeting confirmed: Fri, Jun 18, 2027 — 10:00–11:00 PT (Zoom link in calendar invite).
- Owners:
  - Product scenario & risk wedges — Jonas Weber
  - Sales bookings & renewals sensitivity — Marissa Cole
  - Financial consolidations and decision matrix — Marcus Lin

Pre-work checklist (please confirm by Thu EOD Jun 17):
- Jonas: risk wedge tab in QBR-SCENARIOS-2027.xlsx (row-level assumptions).
- Marissa: bookings sensitivity + two prospect timelines added to the "Sales Assumptions" sheet.
- Vivek: a short note on hiring freezes / ramp timing that would materially change headcount assumptions.
- All: a one-slide summary (single PDF slide) attached to this thread.

Alex Moran at Capital Partners — we're keeping the last 15 minutes of the meeting as an optional external sanity check. If you can prepare 5–10 minutes on how you think ARR expansion tends to play out for partners of your size, that would be valuable but optional.

I'll push a consolidated deck to the Drive morning-of and share the public link in the invite. If you have material constraints that prevent you from completing the pre-work, call me directly so we can either swap owners or table items.

Marcus
